rows: Bicuar National Park is located in South West Angola. The vegetation includes two principal woodland types, miombo and Baikiaea shrub/thicket vegetation. A total of 22 one-hectare forest inventory plots with trees ≥ 5 cm diameter included span a gradient from open grassland to closed thicket/forest vegetation. The past history of included selective logging of timber species. Mid-elevation (c. 1200-1300 m a.s.l.) tropical dry forest and woodland savanna. SEOSAW and ForestPlots.net site.
Francisco Maiato Gonçalves; José Tchamba; António Valter Chisingui; Kyle Dexter; John Godlee
Parque Nacional Bicuar; Instituto Superior de Ciências de Educação da Huíla ISCED-Huíla

The Misiones site is located within the Guarani Multiple Use Reserve (RUMG, Faculty of Forestry Sciences - National University of Misiones). The site includes 18 forest inventory plots, 1 ha size each with all trees, palms and lianas ≥ 10 cm included. Of these, there are 4 control plots, 8 plots with reduced-impact logging, and 6 with conventional logging (first measurement: 1998; logging date: 1999). Lowland (350-500 m a.s.l.) subtropical semideciduous forest. TmFO Site.

Instituto de Biología Subtropical - UNaM CONICET; Facultad de Ciencias Forestales de la Universidad Nacional de Misiones; Universidad Nacional de Misiones; Centro de Investigaciones del Bosque Atlántico - CeIBA

Calperum Mallee is in a mallee semi-arid ecosystem, fringing the River Murray floodplains, near Renmark, South Australia. Eighteen 1-ha permanent inventory plots are established. The area comprises undulating mallee woodlands and riverine vegetation alongside the river; recovering from extensive grazing. The Native Title for the area is held by the First Peoples of the River Murray and Mallee. Lowland (c 60 m a.s.l.) low open mallee woodland. TERN supersite.
Asutrlian Landscape Trust; Government of South Australia

Great Western Woodlands is on Credo Station, a former pastoral property in Western Australia’s Goldfields region, near Kalgoorlie, Western Australia. The region covers 16 million hectares in south-west Western Australia and is the largest remaining intact ‘Mediterranean’ woodland in the world, dominated by Eucalyptus. Thirteen 1-ha permanent inventory plots for trees have been established. Native title claims of traditional ownership at this site have been registered by the Marlinyu Ghoorlie and Maduwongga Peoples. TERN supersite.

Litchfield Savanna is within Litchfield National Park, about 80 km south of Darwin, Northern Territory, in a high rainfall, frequently burnt, tropical savanna—the dominant ecosystem type across northern Australia. Litchfield National Park encompasses the traditional boundaries of 4 Aboriginal language groups: Werat, Koongurrukun, Waray and Mak Mak Marranunggu. Lowland (c. 220 m a.s.l.) tropical savanna. TERN supersite.
The University of Western Australia; Charles Darwin University

Robson Creek Rainforest is on the Atherton Tablelands, in Danbulla National Park, within the Wet Tropics World Heritage area. With a tropical monsoon climate the rainfall is seasonal with approximately 60% falling between January and March. A 25-ha permanent inventory plot has been established. The vegetation is a mix of complex mesophyll, and simple notophyll vine rainforest. The traditional owners in this area are the Tableland Yidinji People. Lowland (c. 720 m a.s.l.) tropical demideciduous forest. TERN supersite and ForestGEO sIte.

Tumbarumba is managed and operated by TERN with valued input from the Forestry Corporation of New South Wales. Located in the Bago State Forest, near Batlow, the site is in open wet sclerophyll Eucalypt forest managed for hardwood timber production. We acknowledge and honour all traditional custodians past and present of this area, including the Wiradjuri and Ngarigo people, who lived and continue to live on this land. Mid-elevation (1250 m a.s.l.) tall temperate forest. TERN supersite.

Assis Ecological Station (EEA), nearby the city of Assis, harbors a remnant of closed-cerrado (cerradão), which once covered much of the area, but was mostly destroyed to give place to sugar cane, and other agronomic commodities. The area of EEA spans about 1700 ha and is located along Rodovaria SP333. One 10.24 ha (320x320 m) plot was established in the late 1990s as part of the project Parcelas Permanente São Paulo (PPSP, BIOTA-FAPESP), and all trees ≥ 5 cm trunk diameter were included. Lowland (c. 550 m a.s.l.) woodland savanna (cerradão). USP/FAPESP site.
Giselda Durigan; Renato Augusto Ferreira de Lima; Natalia Ivanauskas; Matheus Pinheiro Ferreira

Instituto de Pesquisas Ambientais - IPA; Laboratório de Ecologia e Restauração Florestal- LERF; Escola Superior de Agricultura "Luiz de Queiroz" - ESALQ; Universidade de São Paulo - USP; Fundaçao florestal

Caetetus Ecological Station (EEC) spans an area of 2000 ha and is covered with semideciduous forests, a degraded forest ecosystem type in Southern Brazil. These areas were converted for urbanization. Forest structure and tree diversity differs totally from that of the Atlantic Rainforest. One 10.24 ha plot (320x320 m) was established in the late 1990s as part of the project Parcelas Permanente São Paulo (PPSP, BIOTA-FAPESP), and all trees ≥ 5 cm trunk diameter are included. Mid-elevation (500-700 m a.s.l.) tropical semi-deciduous forest. USP/FAPESP site.
Renato Augusto Ferreira de Lima; Natalia Ivanauskas; Matheus Pinheiro Ferreira

Laboratório de Ecologia e Restauração Florestal- LERF; Escola Superior de Agricultura "Luiz de Queiroz" - ESALQ; Universidade de São Paulo - USP; Instituto de Pesquisas Ambientais - IPA; Escola Superior de Agricultura "Luiz de Queiroz" - ESALQ; Universidade de São Paulo - USP; Fundaçao florestal

State Park Carlos Botelho (PECB) is located near the city of São Miguel Arcanjo, Sao Paulo. It harbors one of the best-preserved stretches of the Atlantic rainforest of which about 90% has been destroyed. PEBC spans over 37000 ha, along the SP139 road. One 10.24 ha plot (320x320 m) was established in the late 1990s as part of the project Parcelas Permanente São Paulo (PPSP, BIOTA-FAPESP), and all trees ≥ 5 cm trunk diameter are included. Lowland (300-1000 m a.s.l.) tropical moist forest. USP/FAPESP site.
Renato Augusto Ferreira de Lima; Natalia Ivanauskas; Matheus Pinheiro Ferreira

Laboratório de Ecologia e Restauração Florestal- LERF; Escola Superior de Agricultura "Luiz de Queiroz" - ESALQ; Universidade de São Paulo - USP; Instituto de Pesquisas Ambientais - IPA; Fundaçao florestal

Caxiuanã National Forest spans an area of 300,000 ha of lowland moist Amazonian forest. It is located 400 km from Belém, on the west banks of the Baía de Caxiuanã between the Xingu River and downstream from the Anapu River. The national forest is the oldest in Amazônia Legal, and is also the second oldest national forest in Brazil (1961, Federal Law No. 239). Caxiuanã is noted for its rich biodiversity, geographic isolation, The Ferreira Penna Scientific Station (Estação Científica Ferreira Penna) is maintained by the Museu Paraense Emílio Goeldi and IBAMA, and is the center of many international research projects. ForestPlots site.

Ilha do Cardoso State Park (created 1962) is covered with lowland forest on sandy soil (restinga), near the city of Cananéia. One 10.24 ha plot was established in the 1990s as part of the project Parcelas Permanente São Paulo (PPSP, BIOTA-FAPESP) with all trees ≥ 5 cm in diameter included. Lowland (c. 20 m a.s.l.) tropical white sand forest. USP/FAPESP and ForestGEO site.
Alexandre Adalardo de Oliveira; Matheus Pinheiro Ferreira

Laboratório de Ecologia de Florestas Tropicais; Instituto de Biociências-IB; Universidade de São Paulo - USP; Escola Superior de Agricultura "Luiz de Queiroz" - ESALQ; Universidade de São Paulo - USP; Instituto de Pesquisas Ambientais - IPA
Alexandre Adalardo de Oliveira; Alberto Vicentini

The Nova Xavantina site consists of a multiple plots at the southern edge of Amazonia, around the municipality of Nova Xavantina. All areas are in conservation units, indigenous lands, or legal reserves, without any other use or economic exploitation. Ten one-hectare plots are associated with GEOTREES, five in seasonal forest (diameter ≥ 10 cm) and five in woodland savanna (diameter ≥ 5 cm). Lowland (c. 200-300 m a.s.l.) tropical semi-evergreen forest and woodland savanna (cerradão and cerrado). RAINFOR and ForestPlots.net site.
Universidade do Estado de Mato Grosso

The Peruaçu site is a dry forest located in the Parque Nacional Cavernas do Peruaçu in the North of Minas Gerais (Januária, Itacarambi, São João das Missões). Ten one-hectare plots are associated with GEO-TREES. Lowland (c. 200-300 m a.s.l.) tropical dry forest. ForestPlots.net site.
Mario Marcos do Espírito Santo; Kyle Dexter
Universidade Estadual de Montes Claros; University of Edinburgh

The Bouamir Research Station was established in 1993 in the Dja Faunal Reserve. It is reached by foot via a 7-hour hike, and it includes mixed and swamp forest types. Eight permanent inventory plots of 1 ha each have been established with trees ≥ 10 cm included. Lowland (650 -700 m a.s.l.) tropical moist forest. Cafriplot site.

The Somalomo Research Station is located on the edge of the Dja Faunal Reserve and a 4–5 hour drive from Yaoundé. The site includes monodominant and mixed forest. Fourteen permanent inventory plots of 1 ha each have been established with trees ≥ 10 cm included. Lowland (650 -700 m a.s.l.) tropical moist forest. AfriTRON and ForestPlots.net site.
Université de Yaoundé I - UYI; MINFOF

The Mbalmayo site is located in Mbalmayo Forest Reserve, South of the city of Mbalmayo. Fourteen permanent inventory plots of 1 ha each have been established with trees ≥ 10 cm included. Lowland (660 m a.s.l.) tropical moist forest. Cafriplot site.
Université de Yaoundé I - UYI; École Nationale des Eaux et Forêts du Cameroun - ENEF

The Petawawa Research Forest (PRF) is located near Chalk River, Ontario, northwest of Ottawa. It is managed by the Canadian Forest Service, and was established in 1918 to study silviculture, wildland fire, forest ecology, tree genetics. PRF is Canada’s oldest research forest and its first remote sensing supersite. Dominannt tree species include: white, red and jack pine, red oak, yellow birch, red and sugar maple, and white spruce. Lowland (c. 150 m a.s.l.) temperate forest. Canada supersite.
The Canadian Forest Service - Natural Resources Canada

Amacayacu National Natural Park is located in Colombian Amazonia. The site was established on Tertiary sedimentary plains (Pebas Formation), with a hilly and moderatly dissected topography. One 25 hectare permanent inventory plot was established in 2006, and an additional 1-ha plot will be created in a secondary forest toas part of GEO-TREES. Lowland (c. 100 m a.s.l.) tropical wet forest. ForestGEO site.
Álvaro Duque; Nicolás Castaño Arboleda; Daniel Zuleta
Universidad Nacional Medellin; Parques Nacionales Naturales de Colombia; Instituto Amazónico de Investigaciones Científicas SINCHI

Téné Site is located Southwest of Yamoussoukro as part of a protected area. Ten 4-ha forest inventory plots have been established with all trees ≥ 10 cm diameter inventoried. Lowland (175-220 m a.s.l.) tropical semi-deciduous forest. TmFO site.
Irié Casimir Zo-Bi; Tiodionwa Abdoulaye Ouattara; Goualo Yves Doua Bi
Institut National Polytechnique Félix Houphouët-Boigny- INP-HB; SODEFOR

Luki is within the Luki Biosphere Reserve (33 000ha), located in the Province of Bas-Congo, in the south-west of the Democratic Republic of Congo, about 120 km from the Atlantic coast. It forms the extreme southern tip of the Guinean-Congolese forest massif. Vegetation consists of moist semi-deciduous rainforest with some management in the landscape. Lowland (c. 150-500 m a.s.l.) tropical semi-deciduous forest. INERA and OFVi site.
Institut Nationale pour l'Etude et la Recherche Agronomiques- INERA
CIRAD; Gembloux Agro-Bio Tech - Liège Université

Yangambi is within Yangambi Biosphere Reserve (YBR) of 2300 km2, located in the province of Tshopo in the northeast of Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), c 100 km west of Kisangani. Vegetation consists of moist semi-deciduous rainforest, with patches of moist evergreen rainforest in river valleys, and agricultural land. Lowland (c. 400-500 m a.s.l.) tropical semi-deciduous forest. An INERA station. AfriTRON and ForestPlots.net site.
Dieumerci Assoumani; Jean-Rémy Makana; Bhély Angoboy Ilondea
Institut Nationale pour l'Etude et la Recherche Agronomiques- INERA; Université de Kisangani - UNIKIS
Ghent University; Gembloux Agro-Bio Tech - Liège Université; CIRAD; CENAREST

The Nouragues Ecological Research Station was created in 1986 in an isolated and pristine rain forest, with no selective logging. Since 1996, The Station is under Natural Reserve protection. Three permanent inventory plots with cumulative area of 28 ha including all trees ≥ 10 cm trunk diameter. Lowland (c. 100 m a.s.l.) tropical moist forest. GUYAFOR and ForestPlots.net site.
Centre national de la recherche scientifique- CNRS; Centre de Recherche sur la Biodiversité et l'Environnement- CRBE

The Paracou Research Station is located approximately 50 km NW of Kourou. The site (owned by CNES, granted to CIRAD) is of about 40,000 ha is mainly covered with a 500-ha core area. Fifteen 6.25 ha permanent inventory plots plus one 25 ha have been sruveyed every 1-2 since 1984. Nine of the plots were selectively logged as part of an experiment in 1986. Lowland (c. 20 m a.s.l.) tropical moist forest. GUYAFOR and TmFO site.
CIRAD; UMR EcoFoG; Université de Guyane

The Ipassa Research Station is located around ten kilometres from the town of Makokou, in the Ivindo National Park (Ogooué Ivindo). It managed by IRET (CENAREST). Vegetation has been monitored since 1963 using a network of permanent plots. Twelve permanent inventory plots with trees ≥ 10 cm trunk diameter have been surveyed. Lowland (c. 500 m a.s.l.) tropical moist forest. CENAREST and OFVi site.

Lopé is within Lopé National Park, Gabon, which covers c. 5000 km2 of of protected area since 2002. The area is dominated by tropical forests and grasslands, savannas and shrublands. Lowland (c. 800 m a.s.l.) tropical forest-savanna mosaic. AfriTRON and ForestPlots.net site.
Agence nationale des parcs nationaux - ANPN; Université des Sciences et Techniques de Masuku- USTM
University of Stirling; University of Leeds

The Mondah Forest is a protected coastal forest (6,747 ha) located in the Komo-Mondah department in northwestern Gabon. Also known as the “forest of giants” and located just outside Libreville, it is one of the most studied and environmentally important forests in the country. The area is dominated by tropical forests on sandy soils. Lowland (c. 20m a.s.l.) tropical forest. AfriTRON and ForestPlots.net site.
Agence nationale des parcs nationaux - ANPN; Université des Sciences et Techniques de Masuku- USTM
Forestry Research Institute of Ghana- CSIR-FORIG

Haldwani, Uttarakhand SuperSite belong to Tarai region on the foothills of the lower Shiwaliks, with alluvial fans and is under plantation by the Uttarakhand Forest Department. The area was dominated by extensive moist deciduous Sal (Shorea robusta) forest before its conversion to plantation. The main tree species found in the area are Eucalyptus hybrid (Eucalyptus), Tectona grandis (teak), Populus deltoides (Poplar), and mixed plantations. The monoculture plantations are raised under different age and harvesting regime. The Eucalyptus and poplar are short rotation crops (10-12 yrs) and Teak has rotation period of about 30-40 yrs. Mixed plantation are of different age (young to old growth) and are currently not felled owing to importance of these forests in providing fodder to herbivores. The Haldwani, Uttarakhand SuperSite is stretched by 25 plots of 1ha each. An ISRO supersite, funded as part of the NISAR Science Project.
Space Applications Centre; Indian Institute of Remote Sensing -IIRS

Hoshangabad, Madhya Pradesh SuperSite is located in the Central Indian highlands. This region is characterized by tropical dry deciduous and tropical dry evergreen vegetation, typical of Plains biome. The major tree species of the forests include teak (Tectona grandis), sal (Shorea robusta), neem (Azadirachta indica), peepal (Ficus religiosa), shisham (Dalbergia sissoo) and bamboo (Bambuseae spp.). This area also contains grassland and scrubland vegetation and forest has distinct leaf-on and leaf-off periods. This region is relatively flat with the presence of isolated hills with gentle slopes. 10 plots of 1ha size each compose this BRM Site. An ISRO supersite, funded as part of the NISAR Science Project.
Anup Das; C. Patnaik; D.G. Bairagi

Idamalayar site is located in Sothern Western Ghats, Kerala state. This lower montane region is characterized by a mix of evergreen, semi-evergreen, and moist deciduous (both pure and mixed with reed) forests. Bamboo formations, reeds, and marshy lands are also present in the area. The landscape also includes grasslands, tree savannahs, and various degraded or naturally open formations. Idamalayar site covers 10 to 15 plots of 1ha each. An ISRO supersite, funded as part of the NISAR Science Project.
Anup Das; Girish Gopinath; K.A. Sreejith

Karbi Anglong SuperSite is located in Lower Montaine of the North East Hills in Assam, India. The region is characterized by (1) moist semi-evergreen forests characterize the region, (2) moist mixed deciduous forests, (3) riverine type and (4) miscellaneous type with scattered pure or mixed patches of bamboos. The area is hilly with moderate slopes. Elevation ranges from 90 – 970m asl. This SuperSite is composed of 10 plots of 1ha size each. An ISRO supersite, funded as part of the NISAR Science Project.
Anup Das; C. Patnaik; P.L.N. Raju; Prasanna Boruah

Nilambur SuperSite is located in the Southern Western Ghats in Kerala. This site is a part of the Nilgiri biosphere reserve, famous for Nilambur Teak (Tectona grandis). The Region has deciduous hardwood vegetation and evergreen forests, characterising the Lower Montane. The evergreen forests are more prevalent at higher altitudes. This SuperSite is composed of 10 plots of 1ha size each. An ISRO supersite, funded as part of the NISAR Science Project.
Anup Das; C. Patnaik; Girish Gopinath

Sasan Gir, Gujarat. This SuperSite is part of the Saurashtra region in the Indian western coastal plain. This region has dry deciduous forest. It’s characterized by a mix of deciduous trees, semi-evergreen and evergreen trees, scrub forest, and grasslands. The forest also includes some areas with rocky hills. It is the largest tract of dry deciduous forest in western India. This is the only place on the earth where Asiatic lions can be found in the wild. Sasan Gir-Gujarat SuperSite is composed of 12 plots of 1ha size each. An ISRO supersite funded as part of the NISAR Science Project.
Anup Das; C. Patnaik; Rajkumar Yadav

The Shimoga site is located in the vicinity of Anjanapura water reservoir, in the Western Ghats, Karnataka. This lowland region (600-700 m a.s.l.) is characterized by tropical dry and tropical moist forests with both deciduous and semi-evergreen vegetation. The region has Tectona grandis (teak) and Acacia auriculiformis (acacia) as dominant forest species and several secondary species including Terminalia paniculata and Terminalia tomentosa. Teak and acacia plantations of various age groups (5 to 60 years) are present in the area. The forest has distinct leaf-on and leaf-off period. The moist deciduous forests in the region shed its leaves during the months of December-February and get its foliage back before the monsoon sets in the month of May. This SuperSite is composed of 10 plots of 1ha size each. An ISRO supersite, funded as part of the NISAR Science Project.
Anup Das; C. Patnaik; A.G. Koppad
Space Applications Centre; University of Agricultural Sciences - Dharwad - UASD

Similipal sanctuary is one of the UNESCO-recognized biosphere reserves in India. This tropical moist forest is located on Lower Montane of the Deccan Peninsular Plateau in the state of Odisha. 
 The vegetation is a mix of different forest types and habitats, with Northern tropical moist deciduous dominating some semi-evergreen patches. Sal (Shorea robusta) is the dominant tree species here. The park also has extensive grasslands that are grazing grounds for many of the herbivores. Similipal National Park derives its name from the abundance of Semul or red silk cotton trees that bloom abundantly in the locality. The area in undulating with a range in elevation of 80 to 869 m. Similipal site covers 20 plots of 1 ha each. An ISRO supersite, funded as part of the NISAR Science Project.
Space Applications Centre; National Remote Sensing Centre- NRSC

Tapi forest’s SuperSite is located in Gujarat plains, North West India, at approximately 600m of elevation. This is a dry deciduous forest characterized by an upper canopy at 15–25 meters, a 10-15 meter understory of smaller trees and large shrubs, and a 3-4 meter undergrowth. Teak (Tectona grandis) is the dominant canopy tree, in association with coromandel ebony (Diospyros melanoxylon), dhaora (Anogeissus latifolia), Lagerstroemia parviflora and Terminalia tomentosa. Riparian areas along the rivers and streams, which receive year-round water, supports moist evergreen forests. Many trees lose their leaves during the long dry season to conserve moisture. Tapi forest, Gujarat, SuperSite is composed of 12 plots of 1ha size each. An ISRO supersite funded as part of the NISAR Science Project.
Anup Das; C. Patnaik; Rajkumar Yadav

This site is located in the Yellapur Forest Division on the Western Ghats, Uttara Kannada District of Karnataka.The lowland region (500-600 m a.s.l.) comprises of highly mixed, heterogeneous forest landscape, and varied from dry deciduous forests in the lower rainfall zones to the northeast, transiting to moist deciduous and high rainfall zones of secondary wet evergreen forests to the south and southwest with small patches of primary wet evergreen forests. Yellapur site comprises 10 plots of 1 ha each. An ISRO supersite, funded as part of the NISAR Science Project.
Anup Das; C. Patnaik; A.G. Koppad
Space Applications Centre; University of Agricultural Sciences - Dharwad - UASD

Mpala Research Center is located in Laikipia Plateau, Central Kenya. The area is a semi-arid savanna (Acacia drepanolobium, A. etbaica, and A. mellifera) open to livestock, wild herbivores and carnivores. Herbivory is the main cause of vegetation disturbance. One 120 ha plot (500m x 2400m) was established in 2011 with all trees at diameter at knee height ≥ 2 cm included. Mid-elevation (1660-1800 m a.s.l.) tropical woodland savanna. ForestGEO site.
Duncan M Kimuyu; Paul Mutuku Musili
Karatina University; National Museums of Kenya; The Mpala Wildlife Foundation; Kenya Wildlife Service -KWS

The Danum Valley Field Centre is located in undulating landscape of the Danum Valley Conservation Area. Research includes forest regeneration, carbon dynamics, and biodiversity in adjacent logged forest and forest fragmented by oil palm plantations. One 50-ha permament tree plot was established in 2011 some 1 km west of the Field Centre in the mixed dipterocarp forest. Lowland (below 760 m a.s.l.) moist tropical forest. ForestGEO Site.
South East Asia Rainforest Research Partnership - SEARRP
Aberdeen University; Estación Experimental de Zonas Áridas-EEZA; Sabah Foundation; University of Zurich

Lambir Hills National Park protects close to 7000 ha of mixed dipterocarp forest in Sarawak, Malaysia. A 52-ha permanent plot was established in 1991, and it is covered with lowland (150-430 m a.s.l.) mixed dipterocarp forest. ForestGEO Site.
Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute; Osaka Metropolitan University; Ehime, & Kyoto Universities; Arnold Arboretum of Harvard University

Pasoh site is located in the Pasoh Forest Reserve, a lowland dipterocarp forest. The area is aseasonal and has a flat terrain. One 50 hectare inventory plot was first completed in 1989, with all trees ≥ 1 cm diameter. Lowland (c 100 m a.s.l.) tropical moist forest. ForestGEO Site.
Arnold Arboretum of Harvard University; National Institute of Environmental Studies, Japan - NIES

Sepilok is a forest reserve in Sabah, Malaysia, established in 1931 near the city of Sandakan. The site is owned by the Sepilok Forest Research Centre division of the Sabah Forestry Department. Distinct forest types occur across Sepilok: alluvial dipterocarp forests in the valley bottoms, sandstone dipterocarp forests on dissected hillsides and crests, and heath forests (kerangas) on nutrient-depleted dip slopes. Lowland (50 to 250 m a.s.l.) tropical moist forest. ForestPlots.net site.
Sabah Forestry Department- Forest Research Centre
Agua Salud Station is located in central Panama. One objective of the station is to study reforestation with native species.

Barro Colorado Island (BCI) is located on the Panama Canal Zone and became an island with the creation of Gatun Lake in 1913. A 50-hectare plot was established in 1981, and it is covered with lowland (c. 120 m a.s.l.) tropical moist deciduous forest. ForestGEO Site.
Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute; Field Museum; University of California, Los Angeles - UCLA
Panama Canal Authority; Univeristy of Georgia

Fortuna Field Station is located in western Panama, and is in a protected area. The reserve encompasses an elevational transect from sea level to 1,400 meters on Panama’s Caribbean slope. A total of 13 1-hectare plot was established since 2003, and it is covered with montane (>1000 m a.s.l.) wet tropical forest. ForestGEO Site.

ForestGEO and the New Guinea Binatang Research Center (BRC) have established a 50-ha plot in lowland rainforest in Madang Province, Papua New Guinea, near the village of Wanang. The project is the first study of carbon dynamics in PNG forests and will enable researchers to assess the response of Pacific forests to global change and understand the ecological processes that sustain healthy forest ecosystems in the Pacific region. The forest is diverse and structurally complex with numerous woody vines and a 40-60 m canopy. The vegetation has been classified as mixed evergreen hill forest. Soils are latosols. Size: 50.00ha; Ecological Zone: Tropical rainforest
University of Minnesota; Czech Academy of Sciences

Jenaro Herrera is a research station by IIAP which is located at 3 hour from Iquitos, Peru. The Centre provides services and facilities. A total of 21 (0.5 - 1 ha) permanent inventory plots with trees ≥ 10 cm are surveyed. The majority of the area is undisturbed forest, selective logging activities has been conducted in flooded areas, and some areas are abandoned pastures. Lowland (c 100 m a.s.l. tropical moist forest. RAINFOR, TmFO and ForestPlots.net site
Gabriel Hidalgo Pizango; Euridice Honorio Coronado
Instituto de Investigaciones de la Amazonía Peruana-IIAP; Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew.
University of St Andrews; University of Leeds

Tambopata National Reserve, in Madre de Dios (southeast Peru). A total of eight one-hectare permanent plots were established last century with all stems ≥ 10 cm diameter included. Two more 1-ha plots have been set-up as part of GEOTREES. Lowland (c. 200 m a.s.l.) tropical moist forest. RAINFOR and ForestPlots.net site.
Tim Baker; Oliver Phillips; John Terborgh
University of Leeds; Duke University- Nicholas School of the Environment

The Palanan research station is located in Isabela, Philippines, on the northeast coast of Luzon Island, in the foothills of the Sierra Madre Mountains. A 16-ha plot was initiated in 1994. The site is in the typhoon belt. Lowland (70-120 m a.s.l.) tropical mixed dipterocarp forest. ForestGEO Site.
Lillian Jennifer Rodriguez; Mariano Roy Duya
University of the Philippines Diliman - UPD; Philippine Department of Environment Natural Resources

Loundoungou is located in Toukoulaka Province, Northern Congo. The site is within a forestry concession on clay soils of the Congolese basin, and shows signs of past human disturbances by traditional activities. Four 9-hectare permanent inventory plots with trees ≥ 10 cm have been established. Lowland (c 500 m a.s.l.) moist tropical forest. TmFO and OFVi site.

The Sinharaja World Heritage Site is the largest remaining tract of lowland rainforest in Sri Lanka. Sinhara ja is a mixed-dipterocarp lowland moist forest (424–575 m a.s.l.) The 25-ha Sinharaja site was established in 1993. Sri Lanka’s rainforests exhibit relatively low overall diversity but extremely high endemism. For example, in Sinharaja, 70% of the 190 recorded tree species are endemic. The site itself measures 25 hectares (500 × 500 m). ForestGEO site.

The Huai Kha Khaeng (HKK) Plot spans 50 hectares (1000 m x 500 m) and is situated in central Thailand. The plot's elevation ranges between 549-638 m asl, situated within a stand of dry evergreen forest undisturbed by logging activity. Six censuses have been conducted including 1994, 1999, 2004, 2009, 2014 and 2019. All trees with a diameter at breast height (DBH) of 1 cm or greater were measured. ForestGEO site.

CALL | Postdoctoral Fellowship in Tropical Forest Mortality

The causes and dynamics of tropical tree mortality remain poorly understood, resulting in significant uncertainty in how tropical forests will respond to future environmental changes. Long-term ForestGEO data, coupled with annual mortality surveys, will be used to explore the drivers and dynamics of tree mortality. Additional field data may be needed to advance understanding of mortality (e.g., measurements of plant stress, traits associated with disturbances, fire resistance, drought tolerance, carbon starvation, etc.). The overall goal is to significantly improve model representation of tree mortality in tropical forests.
ForestGEO invites applications for a postdoctoral fellowship in tropical forest mortality working alongside the GEO-TREES team. 
Review of applications will begin on 29 December 2025.

Event | GEO-TREES Gabon Kick-off Meeting and Launch of the Lopé Forest Inventory Campaign

The GEO-TREES Gabon project, part of One Forest Vision Inittative (OFVI) and DISC BIOMASS Project, held its kick-off meeting in Libreville in March 2026, followed by the launch of the forest inventory campaign at La Lopé. Carried out in partnership with CENAREST, ANPN, AGEOS, OFVI, GFZ, CNRS and ESA, the project combines forest inventories with ground-based and airborne lidar at Ipassa, Lopé and Mondah to improve carbon stock estimates for Congo Basin forests.

A research aircraft from the German Aerospace Center (DLR) has been taking radar images of the rainforest – flying paths simultaneously with the European Space Agency's (ESA) Biomass Earth observation satellite.  The measurement flights of the Dornier DO 228-212 D-CFFU were precisely coordinated with the overflights of the new satellite, which has been orbiting Earth since April 2025 to determine global forest biomass using an innovative P-band radar system.  GEO-TREES contributes to this campaign with ground-based measurements of the Lopé, Mondah and Ipassa sites in Gabon.

Site Spotlight | Dr. José Tchamba at Bicuar National Park

Bicuar National Park in Angola lies at the edge of the Miombo ecoregion, an open woodland-grassland mosaic which covers the majority of southern Africa. Bicuar sits on deep, well-drained Kalahari sands soils, featuring seasonally flooded grasslands at the bottom of shallow valleys (mulolas), rising through open woodlands to dense thicket on the hill crests. Bicuar experiences frequent fires, and elephants routinely fell small trees, creating a highly dynamic landscape. Dr. José João Tchamba is a principle investigator (PI) for GEO-TREES and the Director of CEBEA at the Instituto Superior de Ciências de Educação da Huíla (ISCED). He’s researching wildfire ecology, in addition to overseeing species dynamics, and vegetation research at the park. We caught up with José to learn about the research at Bicuar and how he got involved.
